Proposes an evaluation method (benchmark OctoBench + OctoBench-Conflict and an observation-and-scoring toolkit for instruction following in coding scaffolds); secondary: compares (8 models x 3 scaffolds)

No SDD approach. Instruction sources evaluated: system prompt, system reminders, user queries, repository policy files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md), Skill.md, memory files, tool schemas. Scaffolds: Claude Code 2.0.69, Kilo 0.10.2, Droid 0.42.2

Per instance: Docker environment with repository, policy files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md), skill documentation (SKILL.md), optional pre-seeded memory files (e.g. Kilo memory bank), system prompt, multi-turn user queries; binary checklist (avg 32.7 items per instance)

Benchmark: annotators build environment and task specification (seed 72 instances, model-expanded to 217) -> reference agent (GPT-5.1, 16 rollouts) -> LLM checklist generation and consolidation -> joint human-LLM review -> evaluated agent runs with proxy logging -> trajectory normalization -> LLM-judge scoring per check (3 judges) -> ISR/CSR

Instruction-following compliance: Instance Success Rate (ISR, all checks pass) and Check item Success Rate (CSR, mean share of checks passed); per category and per scaffold; conflict resolution rates (which source followed); gains after feedback; ISR by interaction turns; judge rank stability

Automatic: proxy-logged trajectories scored per checklist item by an LLM-judge panel (GPT-5.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro), mean of three; checklists LLM-generated (GPT-5.1) and human-audited (>95% valid)

Criterion: ISR / CSR (avg of 3 judges); 3 runs per instance per model. 217 instances under 3 scaffolds; 8 models; no baseline (benchmark comparison). Held constant: instance environment, checklist, scaffold defaults, temperature 1.0, Docker with network, timeout ~30 min. Acceptance criterion: binary checklist items judged by LLM panel. Repetitions: 3 runs per instance per model. Extra experiments: conflict set (32 instances), feedback-correction on Claude Code partial failures, ISR by turns, judge consistency. Human intervention: none during runs

Large ISR-CSR gap (CSR 79.75-85.64% vs ISR 9.66-28.11%); Claude Opus 4.5 best overall and most robust across scaffolds and turns; Skill.md constraints weakest category, Memory strongest (e.g. Skill ISR Opus 58.45% vs MiniMax-M2.1 12.33% on Claude Code); system prompt beats project docs and user query beats project docs in conflicts, user vs system varies by model; feedback raises ISR by +7.2 to +16.8 points. No significance tests

Distinguished models and scaffolds; judge rankings stable (max one rank difference); no self-preference found. Repeatability: 3 runs, Std across judges reported; dataset and toolkit to be released. Limitations stated: checklist-verifiable compliance only (not open-ended quality); reliance on LLMs for checklists and judging (<5% problematic items, mostly Tool schema and Skill.md); 34 environments and 3 scaffolds; raw traces not released by default

Need for training and evaluation targeting heterogeneous, persistent instruction following; broader scaffold coverage, stronger deterministic checks, robustness against strategic avoidance of conditional requirements; subjective helpfulness under-represented
